delivered.text: Removing the `if (!job) { return { status: 'missing' as const }; }` guard while `job.amount` is still dereferenced means `computeFee(job.amount)` throws a null/undefined dereference when `claim(id)` returns null, and `settle` can no longer return the 'missing' status its callers may switch on, breaking the return-union contract. Re-introduce the guard before computing the fee and keep the 'missing' branch in the return union.

Flipping the debit operand from `job.amount + fee` to `job.amount - fee` reverses the fee direction, debiting the account `fee` less instead of `fee` more and silently under-charging every settlement if the fee is intended to be charged on top of the amount. Confirm the intended fee direction and restore `job.amount + fee` if the fee is a charge added to the amount.

claim(id) can return null, so dereferencing job.amount and job.account now throws a TypeError and silently drops the 'missing' status from the function's return contract. Restore the guard before dereferencing job, e.g. `if (!job) return { status: 'missing' as const };`, and keep 'missing' in the return type.

Changing the debit from `job.amount + fee` to `job.amount - fee` silently debits the account by `2 * fee` less and can push the balance negative for small amounts. Restore `job.amount + fee` unless the fee is intentionally deducted from the amount, in which case confirm the ledger semantics.

The null-check on the result of `claim(id)` was removed, but `job.amount` and `job.account` are still dereferenced unconditionally, so if `claim` returns null/undefined, `computeFee(job.amount)` throws a TypeError and the previous `{ status: 'missing' }` return contract is dropped. Restore the guard before dereferencing `job`.

The debit amount was changed from `job.amount + fee` to `job.amount - fee`, inverting the fee's effect and silently changing the monetary value moved on the ledger. Confirm the fee semantics, and if the original gross-up was correct, restore `job.amount + fee`.

The debit amount was changed from `job.amount + fee` to `job.amount - fee`, inverting the fee sign even though computeFee's contract in src/payments/fees.ts specifies a fee charged on top of the job amount, so subtracting it under-charges the account, drops the processing fee, and debits less than the job amount. Restore the addition with `await ledger.debit(job.account, job.amount + fee);`.

The settlement debit in src/payments/settle.ts was changed from `job.amount + fee` to `job.amount - fee`, but `computeFee` is documented in fees.ts as a fee charged on top of the job amount, so the account is under-debited by 2*fee and for small amounts the fixed +30 floor can make `amount - fee` negative, turning the debit into a credit and corrupting balances. Restore the addition.

In src/payments/settle.ts, the debit amount sign was flipped from `job.amount + fee` to `job.amount - fee` even though computeFee (src/payments/fees.ts) is documented as a fee charged ON TOP of the job amount, so every settlement under-collects and the processing fee is effectively credited back to the payer; for small amounts (amount < round(amount*0.029)+30, i.e. below ~31) the difference becomes negative and ledger.debit credits the account instead of debiting it. Restore the addition with `await ledger.debit(job.account, job.amount + fee);`.
